-- The definition of a usable incident, in one place.
--
-- Two date classes are excluded from every count the dashboard publishes: the
-- 1900-01-01 sentinel that means the parser could not read a date at all, and
-- dates in the future, which are source typos. Both are kept here and labelled
-- rather than filtered, so the exclusion is countable instead of invisible.
--
-- Mirrors the excluded block in build_aggregates.py.

select
    record_id,
    date_day,

    case
        when date_day <= '1901-01-01' then 'date_sentinel'
        when date_day > current_date then 'date_future'
        else 'usable'
    end as date_class,

    date_day > '1901-01-01' and date_day <= current_date as is_usable,

    -- Before the open-data dashboard stream began, coverage is PDF bulletins
    -- only. Comparisons that straddle this line are not like-for-like.
    date_day >= '2022-01-01' as is_post_regime_change

from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_incidents"

-- Every month between the first and last usable incident, with no gaps.
--
-- Built by generating the range rather than by selecting distinct months from the
-- incidents, because a month with no incidents at all would be missing from the
-- second and present in the first. That is the same mistake dim_date avoids for
-- days, and it matters more than it looks: a window function over a series with a
-- missing month silently changes what "three months" or "twelve months back"
-- means, without any error and without any visible gap in a chart.

with bounds as (
    select
        date_trunc('month', min(date_day))::date as first_month,
        date_trunc('month', max(date_day))::date as last_month
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_dated"
    where is_usable
)

select
    month_start,
    year(month_start) as year,
    month(month_start) as month,
    month_start >= '2022-01-01' as is_post_regime_change
from (
    select unnest(range(
        b.first_month::timestamp,
        (b.last_month + interval 1 month)::timestamp,
        interval 1 month
    ))::date as month_start
    from bounds as b
)

-- What share of each incident's time window fell in civil darkness.
--
-- This is a faithful port of _dark_fraction in build_aggregates.py, not a
-- reimplementation. The rule there: walk every minute from start_min to
-- start_min + duration, wrap at 1440, and count the minutes before civil dawn
-- or at/after civil dusk. A closed form would be shorter but would have to
-- special-case the wrap, and the point of this model is that it agrees with the
-- published panel exactly.
--
-- Only usable rows with a parsed, non-sentinel time and a calendar date qualify,
-- which is the same filter and the same inner join the Python does. That lands on
-- the row count the SPA prints as time_darkness_rows_used. The is_usable term is
-- stated rather than left to the calendar join: the four rows it removes have
-- dates outside the calendar range anyway, so relying on the join would give the
-- right answer for the wrong reason.

with usable as (
    select
        i.record_id,
        i.date_day,
        i.start_hour * 60 + i.start_minute as start_min,
        i.duration_minutes,
        c.dawn_minutes,
        c.dusk_minutes
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_incidents" as i
    join (select record_id, is_usable from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_dated") as d using (record_id)
    join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_calendar" as c using (date_day)
    where d.is_usable
      and i.time_parsed
      and not i.time_unknown_sentinel
),

-- A zero-length window is a point in time, so it gets one minute checked
-- rather than an empty range.
spread as (
    select
        record_id,
        dawn_minutes,
        dusk_minutes,
        unnest(range(
            start_min,
            start_min + greatest(duration_minutes, 1)
        )) % 1440 as minute_of_day
    from usable
),

scored as (
    select
        record_id,
        avg(case when minute_of_day < dawn_minutes
                   or minute_of_day >= dusk_minutes
                 then 1.0 else 0.0 end) as dark_fraction
    from spread
    group by record_id
)

select
    u.record_id,
    u.date_day,
    u.start_min,
    u.duration_minutes,
    u.dawn_minutes,
    u.dusk_minutes,
    s.dark_fraction,

    -- The share of that whole day that was civil-dark. An offense whose
    -- dark_fraction sits above its baseline happens in the dark more than
    -- chance alone would put it there.
    1.0 - (u.dusk_minutes - u.dawn_minutes) / 1440.0 as day_dark_baseline,
    s.dark_fraction - (1.0 - (u.dusk_minutes - u.dawn_minutes) / 1440.0) as dark_bend

from usable as u
join scored as s using (record_id)

-- The wide analytic row: one incident, everything known about it.
--
-- Every join here is on record_id and every one is a left join, because the
-- coverage of each enrichment differs and the differences are the interesting
-- part. Topics only exist for narratives that were embedded, so roughly a third
-- of incidents have no topic at all. Filtering them out here would hide that;
-- carrying nulls forward makes it countable in data_profile_summary.

select
    i.* exclude (merge_notes),

    d.date_class,
    d.is_usable,
    d.is_post_regime_change,

    c.dow,
    c.is_weekend,
    c.iso_week,
    c.is_holiday,
    c.holiday_name,
    c.holiday_is_federal,
    c.daylight_minutes,
    c.civil_light_minutes,
    c.moon_illumination,

    w.temp_avg_f,
    w.temp_max_f,
    w.precip_in,
    w.snow_depth_in,
    w.wind_mph,
    w.is_rainy,
    w.is_snowy,
    w.is_hot,

    w.is_freezing,

    k.dark_fraction,
    k.day_dark_baseline,
    k.dark_bend,

    t.topic_id,
    t.topic_prob,
    t.is_noise_topic,
    t.topic_is_confident,

    f.any_firearm_terms,
    f.any_vehicle_mo,
    f.any_items_stolen,
    f.any_substances,

    f.any_outcome_flags,

    f.outcome_flags_recovered,

    dt.narrative_chars,
    dt.narrative is not null and length(trim(dt.narrative)) > 0 as has_narrative

from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_incidents" as i
-- date_day is projected by both of these, so they are narrowed to the columns
-- this model actually wants rather than joined with `using` and left ambiguous.
join (
    select record_id, date_class, is_usable, is_post_regime_change
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_dated"
) as d using (record_id)
left join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_calendar" as c using (date_day)
left join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_weather_daily" as w using (date_day)

    select record_id, dark_fraction, day_dark_baseline, dark_bend
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incident_darkness"
) as k using (record_id)

left join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_narrative_flags" as f using (record_id)
left join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_incident_details" as dt using (record_id)

select
    record_id as unique_field,
    count(*) as n_records

from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
where record_id is not null
group by record_id
having count(*) > 1

select record_id
from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
where record_id is null

-- Does an offense prefer the dark, beyond the fact that nights are dark?
--
-- avg_dark_fraction alone answers nothing: in December almost any hour is dark.
-- The baseline is the share of each incident's own day that was civil-dark, so
-- the bend is the part that season does not explain. Positive means the offense
-- happens in darkness more than chance would put it there.
--
-- Read with the caveat the panel carries: a range report spreads its weight
-- uniformly, so offenses that are typically discovered later rather than
-- witnessed live will read as darker than they were.

select
    offense,
    count(*) as incidents,
    avg(dark_fraction) as avg_dark_fraction,
    avg(day_dark_baseline) as avg_dark_baseline,
    avg(dark_bend) as avg_dark_bend,
    count(*) filter (where dark_fraction = 1.0) as fully_dark_incidents,
    count(*) filter (where dark_fraction = 0.0) as fully_light_incidents,
    avg(duration_minutes) as avg_window_minutes,
    count(*) filter (where duration_minutes = 0) as point_in_time_incidents
from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
where is_usable
  and dark_fraction is not null
  and offense is not null
group by offense
having count(*) >= 25

-- The hour-by-weekday heatmap, 168 cells, weighted the way the panel weights it.
--
-- An incident reported as "1500-1800 HRS" did not happen at 15:00. The published
-- heatmap spreads a range uniformly across the hours it covers, so three hours of
-- uncertainty contribute a third of an incident each rather than a whole one to
-- the first hour. Point-in-time reports contribute 1.0.
--
-- Faithful port of _hour_dow_matrix in build_aggregates.py. Spreading per minute
-- and dividing is the same arithmetic as its per-hour weights, and it keeps the
-- overnight wrap in one place.

with usable as (
    select
        record_id,
        day_of_week,
        start_hour * 60 + start_minute as start_min,
        duration_minutes,
        time_is_range,
        offense
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable
      and time_parsed
      and not time_unknown_sentinel
),

points as (
    select day_of_week, start_min // 60 % 24 as hour_of_day, offense, 1.0 as weight
    from usable
    where not time_is_range or duration_minutes = 0
),

ranges as (
    select
        day_of_week,
        (unnest(range(start_min, start_min + duration_minutes)) % 1440) // 60 as hour_of_day,
        offense,
        1.0 / duration_minutes as weight
    from usable
    where time_is_range and duration_minutes > 0
),

combined as (
    select * from points
    union all
    select * from ranges
),

grid as (
    select
        d.dow as day_of_week,
        h.hour_of_day
    from (select unnest(range(0, 7)) as dow) as d
    cross join (select unnest(range(0, 24)) as hour_of_day) as h
)

select
    g.day_of_week,
    g.hour_of_day,
    coalesce(sum(c.weight), 0) as weighted_incidents,
    coalesce(count(distinct c.offense), 0) as distinct_offenses
from grid as g
left join combined as c
    on c.day_of_week = g.day_of_week
   and c.hour_of_day = g.hour_of_day
group by g.day_of_week, g.hour_of_day

-- Monthly volume per offense, on a gapless month series.
--
-- The series has to be dense before any window touches it. `rows between 2
-- preceding` and `lag(12)` count ROWS, not months, so on a sparse series they
-- quietly mean something else: for an offense reported in six scattered months
-- across eight years, lag(12) reaches back years rather than one year. Measured on
-- the sparse version of this model, 1,197 of 2,130 year-over-year values did not
-- actually point twelve months back, and nothing about the output looked wrong.
--
-- Each offense is densified from its own first appearance rather than from the
-- start of the dataset. A zero after an offense first appears is a real
-- observation: it did not happen that month. A zero before it ever appeared would
-- imply the same thing about a period when the category may not have been in use
-- at all, which the 2022 ingestion change makes a live risk.

with monthly as (
    select
        date_trunc('month', date_day)::date as month_start,
        offense,
        count(*) as incidents
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable and offense is not null
    group by 1, 2
),

first_seen as (
    select offense, min(month_start) as first_month
    from monthly
    group by offense
),

grid as (
    select f.offense, s.month_start, s.is_post_regime_change
    from first_seen as f
    join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_month_spine" as s
        on s.month_start >= f.first_month
),

dense as (
    select
        g.offense,
        g.month_start,
        g.is_post_regime_change,
        coalesce(m.incidents, 0) as incidents
    from grid as g
    left join monthly as m
        on m.offense = g.offense
       and m.month_start = g.month_start
),

month_totals as (
    select month_start, sum(incidents) as month_incidents
    from monthly
    group by month_start
)

select
    d.month_start,
    d.offense,
    d.incidents,
    t.month_incidents,
    case when t.month_incidents > 0
         then d.incidents * 1.0 / t.month_incidents end as share_of_month,

    -- Three real months of context, because the series is gapless.
    avg(d.incidents) over (
        partition by d.offense order by d.month_start
        rows between 2 preceding and current row
    ) as incidents_3mo_avg,

    -- Exactly twelve months back, for the same reason.
    lag(d.incidents, 12) over (
        partition by d.offense order by d.month_start
    ) as incidents_same_month_last_year,

    d.is_post_regime_change

from dense as d
left join month_totals as t on t.month_start = d.month_start

-- How precise are the dashboard timestamps really?
--
-- The open-data stream carries an exact occur_datetime, which invites treating it
-- as a real instant. It is not always one. Times pile up on round values far
-- beyond what any real distribution would produce: exactly midnight and exactly
-- noon each carry roughly fifty times the uniform per-minute rate, and every
-- on-the-hour value is elevated.
--
-- Midnight and noon are the signature of a date-only record, or of a form that
-- defaults to 12:00 AM. They are almost certainly not 517 incidents that happened
-- at the same instant.
--
-- One row per distinct time-of-day value that clears the clustering threshold, so
-- the reader can see the shape rather than take the caveat on trust.

with timed as (
    select cast(occur_datetime as time) as time_of_day
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable
      and occur_datetime is not null
),

totals as (
    select
        count(*) as timestamped_incidents,
        count(*) / 1440.0 as uniform_per_minute
    from timed
),

counted as (
    select time_of_day, count(*) as incidents
    from timed
    group by time_of_day
)

select
    c.time_of_day,
    date_part('hour', c.time_of_day) as hour_of_day,
    date_part('minute', c.time_of_day) as minute_of_hour,
    c.incidents,
    t.timestamped_incidents,
    c.incidents / t.uniform_per_minute as times_uniform_rate,
    date_part('minute', c.time_of_day) = 0 as is_on_the_hour,
    c.time_of_day in ('00:00:00', '12:00:00') as is_midnight_or_noon
from counted as c
cross join totals as t
where c.incidents >= t.uniform_per_minute * 3

-- One row per calendar day in range, whether or not anything happened on it.
--
-- Days with zero incidents are the reason this is a left join from the calendar
-- rather than a group-by over incidents. A rate denominator that silently skips
-- quiet days overstates every rate built on it.

with daily_counts as (
    select
        date_day,
        count(*) as incidents,
        count(*) filter (where zone_id is not null) as incidents_zoned,
        count(*) filter (where any_vehicle_mo) as incidents_vehicle_mo,
        count(*) filter (where outcome_flags_arrest) as incidents_with_arrest,
        avg(dark_fraction) as avg_dark_fraction
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable
    group by date_day
)

select
    c.date_day,
    c.year,
    c.month,
    c.day,
    c.dow,
    c.is_weekend,
    c.iso_week,
    c.doy,
    c.is_holiday,
    c.holiday_name,
    c.holiday_is_federal,
    c.dawn_minutes,
    c.sunrise_minutes,
    c.sunset_minutes,
    c.dusk_minutes,
    c.daylight_minutes,
    c.civil_light_minutes,
    c.moon_age_days,
    c.moon_illumination,

    w.station_id,
    w.temp_avg_f,
    w.temp_min_f,
    w.temp_max_f,
    w.precip_in,
    w.snow_depth_in,
    w.wind_mph,
    w.humidity_pct,
    w.is_rainy,
    w.is_snowy,
    w.is_hot,
    w.is_cold,
    w.is_freezing,
    w.date_day is null as missing_weather,

    coalesce(d.incidents, 0) as incidents,
    coalesce(d.incidents_zoned, 0) as incidents_zoned,
    coalesce(d.incidents_vehicle_mo, 0) as incidents_vehicle_mo,
    coalesce(d.incidents_with_arrest, 0) as incidents_with_arrest,
    d.avg_dark_fraction,

    c.date_day >= '2022-01-01' as is_post_regime_change

from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_calendar" as c
left join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_weather_daily" as w using (date_day)
left join daily_counts as d using (date_day)

-- Characteristics: numbers that surprise people and are nonetheless correct.
--
-- These are the questions that get asked about the dataset every time someone new
-- looks at it. Answering them here, next to the defect list rather than inside it,
-- is the point: a third of incidents having no topic is not a bug, it is what
-- happens when a third of incidents arrive without narrative text.
--
-- Classes overlap on purpose and do not sum to the row count.

with rows_all as (
    select * from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
),

totals as (
    select
        count(*) as all_rows,
        count(*) filter (where is_usable) as usable_rows
    from rows_all
),

facts as (
    select 'usable_rows' as characteristic, count(*) as row_count,
        'Rows that survive the date filters and back every published count.' as detail
    from rows_all where is_usable
    union all
    select 'source_pdf_only', count(*),
        'Only the PDF activity bulletin reported this incident.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and source = 'pdf'
    union all
    select 'source_dashboard_only', count(*),
        'Only the open-data dashboard reported it. Mostly post-2022, and the reason both streams exist.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and source = 'dashboard'
    union all
    select 'source_both', count(*),
        'Both streams reported it and upstream merged them on the complaint number.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and source = 'both'
    union all
    select 'has_narrative', count(*),
        'Rows with narrative text. Everything downstream of language, topics and flags alike, can only see these.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and has_narrative
    union all
    select 'no_narrative', count(*),
        'Rows with no narrative. Dashboard-only incidents arrive as structured NIBRS charges with no prose.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and not has_narrative
    union all
    select 'topic_assigned', count(*),
        'Narratives BERTopic placed in a theme, noise bucket included.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and topic_id is not null
    union all
    select 'topic_noise', count(*),
        'Narratives BERTopic declined to cluster. A real answer about the text, not a failure.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and is_noise_topic
    union all
    select 'topic_unassigned', count(*),
        'No topic row at all, because there was no narrative to embed.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and topic_id is null
    union all
    select 'zone_assigned', count(*),
        'Incidents inside one of the eight policing zone polygons.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and zone_id is not null
    union all
    select 'zone_unassigned', count(*),
        'Geocoded outside every zone polygon, or not geocoded at all. An Oak Park address on a boundary street can land just outside.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and zone_id is null
    union all
    select 'time_window_is_range', count(*),
        'Reported as a span rather than a moment. The heatmap spreads these across the hours they cover.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and time_is_range
    union all
    select 'time_unknown_sentinel', count(*),
        'Time recorded as unknown. Excluded from every hour-of-day and darkness measure.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and time_unknown_sentinel
    union all
    select 'time_overnight_window', count(*),
        'Time window crosses midnight, so the hour arithmetic has to wrap.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and time_is_overnight
    union all
    select 'post_regime_change', count(*),
        'On or after 2022-01-01, when open-data ingestion began. Before that, coverage is PDF bulletins only.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and is_post_regime_change
    union all
    select 'multi_charge_incidents', count(*),
        'NIBRS incidents carrying more than one charge, collapsed upstream into one row with arrays.'
    from rows_all where is_usable and charge_count > 1
)

select
    f.characteristic,
    f.row_count,
    case when t.usable_rows > 0 then f.row_count * 100.0 / t.usable_rows end as pct_of_usable,
    f.detail
from facts as f
cross join totals as t

-- One row per offense label, with the NIBRS classification it usually carries
-- and how its incidents distribute over time and darkness.
--
-- An offense label can appear under more than one NIBRS crime-against group
-- across incidents, so the group here is the modal one and nibrs_group_count
-- says whether that was a real choice or a foregone conclusion.

with by_offense as (
    select
        offense,
        count(*) as incidents,
        count(*) filter (where is_post_regime_change) as incidents_post_regime,
        count(distinct primary_crime_against) as nibrs_group_count,
        mode(primary_crime_against) as modal_crime_against,
        mode(primary_offense_type) as modal_offense_type,
        mode(primary_nibrs_code) as modal_nibrs_code,
        count(*) filter (where source = 'pdf') as from_pdf_only,
        count(*) filter (where source = 'dashboard') as from_dashboard_only,
        count(*) filter (where source = 'both') as from_both,
        min(date_day) as first_incident,
        max(date_day) as last_incident,
        avg(dark_fraction) as avg_dark_fraction,
        avg(day_dark_baseline) as avg_dark_baseline,
        avg(dark_bend) as avg_dark_bend,
        count(*) filter (where outcome_flags_arrest) as incidents_with_arrest,
        count(*) filter (where has_narrative) as incidents_with_narrative
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable
      and offense is not null
    group by offense
)

select
    offense,
    incidents,
    incidents_post_regime,
    modal_crime_against,
    modal_offense_type,
    modal_nibrs_code,
    nibrs_group_count,
    nibrs_group_count > 1 as spans_multiple_nibrs_groups,
    from_pdf_only,
    from_dashboard_only,
    from_both,
    first_incident,
    last_incident,
    incidents_with_arrest,
    incidents_with_narrative,
    avg_dark_fraction,
    avg_dark_baseline,
    avg_dark_bend
from by_offense

-- One row per BERTopic cluster, with its display words and what it caught.
--
-- Topic -1 is BERTopic's noise bucket, not a theme. It is kept because the size
-- of it is a real measure of how much narrative text would not cluster, and
-- dropping it here would make the topic shares add to more than the corpus.

with words as (
    select
        topic_id,
        string_agg(word, ', ' order by word_rank) as top_words,
        count(*) as word_count,
        max(weight) as top_word_weight
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_topic_words"
    group by topic_id
),

assigned as (
    select
        topic_id,
        count(*) as incidents,
        avg(topic_prob) as avg_topic_prob,
        count(*) filter (where topic_is_confident) as confident_incidents,
        min(date_day) as first_incident,
        max(date_day) as last_incident,
        mode(offense) as modal_offense,
        mode(zone_name) as modal_zone,
        avg(dark_fraction) as avg_dark_fraction,
        count(*) filter (where any_vehicle_mo) as incidents_vehicle_mo
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable and topic_id is not null
    group by topic_id
),

corpus as (
    select count(*) as topic_assigned_incidents
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable and topic_id is not null
)

select
    a.topic_id,
    a.topic_id = -1 as is_noise_topic,
    w.top_words,
    w.word_count,
    w.top_word_weight,
    a.incidents,
    a.incidents * 1.0 / c.topic_assigned_incidents as share_of_assigned,
    a.confident_incidents,
    a.avg_topic_prob,
    a.modal_offense,
    a.modal_zone,
    a.avg_dark_fraction,
    a.incidents_vehicle_mo,
    a.first_incident,
    a.last_incident,
    w.topic_id is null as missing_display_words
from assigned as a
left join words as w using (topic_id)
cross join corpus as c

-- One row per policing zone: geometry, who lives there, and what was reported.
--
-- Per-capita rates use the zone's own ACS population. They are not comparable to
-- a Village-wide rate computed from zone_id 0, because the tract-to-zone
-- allocation double counts residents on shared tract boundaries: the eight zone
-- populations sum to slightly more than the Village rollup. int_zone_reference
-- keeps the rollup out of this table for that reason.

with counts as (
    select
        zone_id,
        count(*) as incidents,
        count(*) filter (where is_post_regime_change) as incidents_post_regime,
        count(distinct date_day) as active_days,
        count(*) filter (where any_vehicle_mo) as incidents_vehicle_mo,
        count(*) filter (where outcome_flags_arrest) as incidents_with_arrest,
        avg(dark_fraction) as avg_dark_fraction,
        min(date_day) as first_incident,
        max(date_day) as last_incident
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable
      and zone_id is not null
    group by zone_id
)

select
    z.zone_id,
    z.zone_name,
    z.area_sq_mi,
    z.tracts_included,
    z.population,
    z.households,
    z.density_per_sq_mi,
    z.median_household_income,
    z.median_age,
    z.pct_white,
    z.pct_black,
    z.pct_asian,
    z.pct_hispanic_any_race,
    z.pct_under_18,
    z.pct_18_64,
    z.pct_65_plus,
    z.pct_owner_occupied,
    z.missing_demographics,

    coalesce(c.incidents, 0) as incidents,
    coalesce(c.incidents_post_regime, 0) as incidents_post_regime,
    coalesce(c.active_days, 0) as active_days,
    coalesce(c.incidents_vehicle_mo, 0) as incidents_vehicle_mo,
    coalesce(c.incidents_with_arrest, 0) as incidents_with_arrest,
    c.avg_dark_fraction,
    c.first_incident,
    c.last_incident,

    case when z.population > 0
         then coalesce(c.incidents, 0) * 1000.0 / z.population end
        as incidents_per_1k_residents,
    case when z.area_sq_mi > 0
         then coalesce(c.incidents, 0) / z.area_sq_mi end
        as incidents_per_sq_mi

from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_zone_reference" as z
left join counts as c using (zone_id)

-- Every gazetteer flag, unpivoted, with how often it fires.
--
-- The wide table is the right shape for the SPA to filter on and the wrong shape
-- for asking which flags are rare. Unpivoting here answers that in one place
-- without a 49-branch union, and the family prefix in each column name becomes a
-- column of its own.
--
-- Denominator is incidents that have narrative text. A flag can only fire on text
-- that exists, so measuring prevalence over all incidents would understate every
-- flag by the share of narrative-free rows.
--
-- The terms behind each flag are private to the pipeline. Only the names are here.

with unpivoted as (
    unpivot (
        select f.*, i.is_usable, i.has_narrative, i.is_post_regime_change
        from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_narrative_flags" as f
        join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched" as i using (record_id)
    )
    on columns(* exclude (record_id, gazetteer_version, is_usable, has_narrative, is_post_regime_change))
    into name flag_name value flag_value
),

scored as (
    select
        flag_name,
        case
            when flag_name like 'any_%' then 'rollup'
            when flag_name like 'firearm_terms_%' then 'firearm_terms'
            when flag_name like 'vehicle_mo_%' then 'vehicle_mo'
            when flag_name like 'items_stolen_%' then 'items_stolen'
            when flag_name like 'substances_%' then 'substances'
            when flag_name like 'location_types_%' then 'location_types'
            when flag_name like 'outcome_flags_%' then 'outcome_flags'
            else 'other'
        end as flag_family,
        count(*) filter (where has_narrative) as narratives_scanned,
        count(*) filter (where flag_value and has_narrative) as flag_hits,
        count(*) filter (where flag_value and has_narrative and is_post_regime_change)
            as flag_hits_post_regime
    from unpivoted
    where is_usable
    group by flag_name
)

select
    flag_name,
    flag_family,
    flag_name like 'any_%' as is_rollup,
    narratives_scanned,
    flag_hits,
    flag_hits_post_regime,
    case when narratives_scanned > 0
         then flag_hits * 1.0 / narratives_scanned end as prevalence,
    flag_hits = 0 as never_fires
from scored

select offense
from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."agg_darkness_by_offense"
where offense is null

select
    offense as unique_field,

-- Mean incidents per day inside each weather cohort, against the all-days mean.
--
-- These cohorts are NOT a partition. A day can be rainy and cold and windy at
-- once, so the rows here overlap and their day counts do not sum to the number
-- of days in range. Anything that adds these rows together is wrong. Each row is
-- only comparable to the baseline row, never to its siblings.
--
-- The denominator is days, not incidents, and it comes from dim_date so that
-- days with zero incidents are counted. A cohort mean computed over only the
-- days something happened would read high for every cohort.

with days as (
    select * from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."dim_date"
    where not missing_weather
      and date_day <= current_date
),

baseline as (
    select
        'all_days' as cohort,
        'baseline' as cohort_kind,
        count(*) as days,
        sum(incidents) as incidents,
        avg(incidents) as mean_incidents_per_day,
        avg(avg_dark_fraction) as mean_dark_fraction
    from days
),

cohorts as (
    select 'rainy' as cohort, 'precipitation' as cohort_kind, * from days where is_rainy
    union all
    select 'snowy', 'precipitation', * from days where is_snowy
    union all
    select 'hot', 'temperature', * from days where is_hot
    union all
    select 'cold', 'temperature', * from days where is_cold
    union all
    select 'freezing', 'temperature', * from days where is_freezing
    union all
    select 'holiday', 'calendar', * from days where is_holiday
    union all
    select 'weekend', 'calendar', * from days where is_weekend
),

summarised as (
    select
        cohort,
        cohort_kind,
        count(*) as days,
        sum(incidents) as incidents,
        avg(incidents) as mean_incidents_per_day,
        avg(avg_dark_fraction) as mean_dark_fraction
    from cohorts
    group by cohort, cohort_kind
),

    select * from baseline
    union all
    select * from summarised
)

    c.cohort_kind,
    c.days,
    c.incidents,
    c.mean_incidents_per_day,
    c.mean_dark_fraction,

    case when b.mean_incidents_per_day > 0

-- Does dbt agree with what the front end printed?
--
-- build_aggregates.py computes in pandas and writes the published JSON. These
-- models recompute the same things from the same artifacts in SQL. Where the two
-- agree, a published number is corroborated by an independent implementation
-- rather than merely asserted. Where they do not, one of them is wrong, and this
-- names which measure to look at.
--
-- Two kinds of check, and the difference matters:
--
--   count  a row count. Cheap, and catches a filter that drifted.
--   value  the output of a rule that had to be reimplemented, compared number
--          for number. This is the one that actually tests a port.
--
-- Counts alone are a weak check. The heatmap weighting and the darkness fraction
-- are both transformations that can be badly wrong while conserving every count:
-- move weight between hours, or mis-wrap an overnight window, and the row count
-- is identical. Only comparing the values catches that.
--
-- Value rows carry a tolerance, because the published JSON rounds. The darkness
-- panel rounds to three decimals and the heatmap to two, so those are the floors
-- below which a difference means nothing.

with published as (
    select * from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_coverage_summary"
),

recounted as (
    select
        count(*) as total_rows,
        count(*) filter (where is_usable) as valid_rows,
        count(*) filter (where date_class = 'date_sentinel') as year_1900_sentinel,
        count(*) filter (where date_class = 'date_future') as future_dates
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_dated"
),

zones as (
    select
        count(*) filter (where i.zone_id is not null) as zone_assigned_rows,
        count(*) filter (where i.zone_id is null) as zone_unassigned_rows
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_incidents" as i
    join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_dated" as d using (record_id)
    where d.is_usable
),

darkness as (
    select count(*) as time_darkness_rows_used
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incident_darkness"
),

days as (
    select
        (select count(*) from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_calendar") as calendar_days,
        (select count(*) from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_weather_daily") as weather_days_used
),

counts as (
    select 'total_rows' as measure, p.total_rows::double as published_value,
           r.total_rows::double as dbt_value
    from published as p cross join recounted as r
    union all
    select 'valid_rows', p.valid_rows, r.valid_rows
    from published as p cross join recounted as r
    union all
    select 'year_1900_sentinel', p.year_1900_sentinel, r.year_1900_sentinel
    from published as p cross join recounted as r
    union all
    select 'future_dates', p.future_dates, r.future_dates
    from published as p cross join recounted as r
    union all
    select 'zone_assigned_rows', p.zone_assigned_rows, z.zone_assigned_rows
    from published as p cross join zones as z
    union all
    select 'zone_unassigned_rows', p.zone_unassigned_rows, z.zone_unassigned_rows
    from published as p cross join zones as z
    union all
    select 'time_darkness_rows_used', p.time_darkness_rows_used, k.time_darkness_rows_used
    from published as p cross join darkness as k
    union all
    select 'calendar_days', p.calendar_days, d.calendar_days
    from published as p cross join days as d
    union all
    select 'weather_days_used', p.weather_days_used, d.weather_days_used
    from published as p cross join days as d
),

-- Value checks. The overall darkness figures compare directly.
dark_overall as (
    select
        pd.published_dark_fraction,
        pd.published_baseline,
        pd.published_bend,
        (select avg(dark_fraction) from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incident_darkness") as dbt_fraction,
        (select avg(day_dark_baseline) from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incident_darkness") as dbt_baseline,
        (select avg(dark_bend) from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incident_darkness") as dbt_bend
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_published_darkness" as pd
    where pd.offense = '__overall__'
),

-- Per-offense darkness collapses to its worst disagreement, so one row says
-- whether any of the ten published offenses drifted.
dark_by_offense as (
    select
        max(abs(p.published_dark_fraction - a.avg_dark_fraction)) as max_fraction_diff,
        count(*) filter (where p.published_incidents <> a.incidents) as count_mismatches,
        count(*) as compared
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_published_darkness" as p
    join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."agg_darkness_by_offense" as a on a.offense = p.offense
    where p.offense <> '__overall__'
),

-- Same for the 168 heatmap cells. A total that matches proves nothing about
-- where the weight landed, so the cells are compared individually.
heatmap as (
    select
        max(abs(p.published_weight - a.weighted_incidents)) as max_cell_diff,
        count(*) filter (where abs(p.published_weight - a.weighted_incidents) > 0.01) as cells_off,
        count(*) as compared
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."stg_published_heatmap" as p
    join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."agg_incidents_by_hour_dow" as a
        on a.day_of_week = p.day_of_week
       and a.hour_of_day = p.hour_of_day
),

values_ as (
    select 'darkness_overall_fraction' as measure,
           published_dark_fraction as published_value, dbt_fraction as dbt_value
    from dark_overall
    union all
    select 'darkness_overall_baseline', published_baseline, dbt_baseline from dark_overall
    union all
    select 'darkness_overall_bend', published_bend, dbt_bend from dark_overall
    union all
    select 'darkness_by_offense_max_diff', 0.0, max_fraction_diff from dark_by_offense
    union all
    select 'darkness_by_offense_count_mismatches', 0.0, count_mismatches from dark_by_offense
    union all
    select 'heatmap_max_cell_diff', 0.0, max_cell_diff from heatmap
    union all
    select 'heatmap_cells_beyond_tolerance', 0.0, cells_off from heatmap
),

combined as (
    select measure, 'count' as check_kind, published_value, dbt_value, 0.0 as tolerance
    from counts
    union all
    select measure, 'value', published_value, dbt_value,
           case
               when measure like 'heatmap_max_cell_diff' then 0.011
               when measure like 'heatmap_cells_beyond_tolerance' then 0.0
               when measure like 'darkness_by_offense_count_mismatches' then 0.0
               else 0.0011

    from values_
)

-- out of the data means a month with no incidents anywhere in the village is

with months as (

),

    g.zone_id,

),

grid as (
    select f.topic_id, s.month_start, s.is_post_regime_change
    from first_seen as f
    join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_month_spine" as s
        on s.month_start >= f.first_month
),

dense as (
    select
        g.topic_id,
        g.month_start,
        g.is_post_regime_change,
        coalesce(m.incidents, 0) as incidents,
        coalesce(m.confident_incidents, 0) as confident_incidents,
        m.avg_topic_prob
    from grid as g
    left join monthly as m
        on m.topic_id = g.topic_id
       and m.month_start = g.month_start
),

month_totals as (
    select month_start, sum(incidents) as month_assigned_incidents
    from monthly
    group by month_start
)

select
    d.month_start,
    d.topic_id,
    t.is_noise_topic,
    t.top_words,
    d.incidents,
    d.confident_incidents,
    d.avg_topic_prob,
    x.month_assigned_incidents,
    case when x.month_assigned_incidents > 0
         then d.incidents * 1.0 / x.month_assigned_incidents end as share_of_month_assigned,
    avg(d.incidents) over (
        partition by d.topic_id order by d.month_start
        rows between 2 preceding and current row
    ) as incidents_3mo_avg,
    d.is_post_regime_change
from dense as d
left join month_totals as x on x.month_start = d.month_start
left join "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."dim_topic" as t on t.topic_id = d.topic_id

with validation_errors as (

    select
        month_start, zone_id
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."agg_incidents_by_zone_month"
    group by month_start, zone_id
    having count(*) > 1

)

select *
from validation_errors

with validation_errors as (

    select
        month_start, topic_id
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."agg_topic_trends"
    group by month_start, topic_id
    having count(*) > 1

)

select *
from validation_errors

-- The densified trend marts must still add up to what went into them.
--
-- Densifying a sparse series to make window functions correct means generating
-- rows, and generating rows is exactly how a grid join goes wrong: a duplicate in
-- the spine or a many-to-many join inflates every total silently, because the
-- shape of the output still looks right.
--
-- Same discipline as assert_hour_dow_weight_conserved. The transformation is
-- allowed to add zeros and nothing else, so the sum before and after must match.

with offense_expected as (
    select count(*) as n
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable and offense is not null
),

offense_actual as (
    select sum(incidents) as n from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."agg_offense_trends"
),

topic_expected as (
    select count(*) as n
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable and topic_id is not null
),

topic_actual as (
    select sum(incidents) as n from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."agg_topic_trends"
),

zone_expected as (
    select count(*) as n
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable and zone_id is not null
),

zone_actual as (
    select sum(incidents) as n from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."agg_incidents_by_zone_month"
),

checks as (
    select 'agg_offense_trends' as mart, e.n as expected, a.n as actual
    from offense_expected as e cross join offense_actual as a
    union all
    select 'agg_topic_trends', e.n, a.n
    from topic_expected as e cross join topic_actual as a
    union all
    select 'agg_incidents_by_zone_month', e.n, a.n
    from zone_expected as e cross join zone_actual as a
)

select mart, expected, actual, actual - expected as difference
from checks
where expected <> actual

-- Defects only: things that are wrong and could in principle be fixed.
--
-- Deliberately separate from data_profile_summary, which holds the numbers that
-- are surprising but correct. Mixing the two produces a defect count that grows
-- every time the dataset gets more interesting, which trains everyone to ignore
-- it.
--
-- One row per defect class. The classes are not disjoint: an incident can be both
-- ungeocoded and date-mismatched, so summing incident_count across rows
-- overstates the number of affected incidents. Where a single number is needed,
-- count distinct records, not classes.

with rows_all as (
    select * from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
),

totals as (
    select count(*) as all_rows from rows_all
),

date_defects as (
    select
        'date_sentinel' as defect_class,
        'incident' as grain,
        count(*) as defect_count,
        'The date parser could not read a date at all and fell back to 1900-01-01.' as detail
    from rows_all where date_class = 'date_sentinel'
    union all
    select 'date_future', 'incident', count(*),
        'Reported date is later than today, which means a typo at the source.'
    from rows_all where date_class = 'date_future'
    union all
    select 'pdf_dashboard_date_mismatch', 'incident', count(*),
        'The PDF bulletin and the open-data dashboard disagree on the date by at least a day. Upstream keeps the PDF date and flags the row.'
    from rows_all where date_mismatch
),

geocode_defects as (
    select 'ungeocoded' as defect_class, 'incident' as grain, count(*) as defect_count,
        'No coordinates, so the incident cannot be placed on the map or assigned to a zone.' as detail
    from rows_all where is_usable and lat is null
),

weather_defects as (
    select 'weather_gap_days' as defect_class, 'day' as grain, count(*) as defect_count,
        'Calendar days in range with no station observation. Any per-day weather cohort silently excludes these.' as detail
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."dim_date"
    where missing_weather and date_day <= current_date
),

flag_defects as (
    select 'dead_gazetteer_flag' as defect_class, 'flag' as grain, count(*) as defect_count,
        'Gazetteer flags that never fire on any narrative. Either the terms never appear in this corpus or the pattern is wrong.' as detail
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."agg_flag_prevalence"
    where never_fires
),

topic_defects as (
    select 'topic_missing_display_words' as defect_class, 'topic' as grain, count(*) as defect_count,
        'Topics carrying incidents but no display words, so the SPA has nothing to label them with.' as detail
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."dim_topic"
    where missing_display_words and not is_noise_topic
),

time_defects as (
    select 'midnight_or_noon_timestamp' as defect_class, 'incident' as grain, count(*) as defect_count,
        'Dashboard timestamps landing exactly on 00:00 or 12:00, at roughly fifty times the uniform per-minute rate. Almost certainly date-only or defaulted entries rather than incidents at that instant.' as detail
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."int_incidents_enriched"
    where is_usable
      and occur_datetime is not null
      and cast(occur_datetime as time) in ('00:00:00', '12:00:00')
),

zone_defects as (
    select 'zone_missing_demographics' as defect_class, 'zone' as grain, count(*) as defect_count,
        'Published zone polygons with no ACS row, which makes a per-capita rate impossible for that zone.' as detail
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."dim_zone"
    where missing_demographics
),

parity_defects as (
    select 'published_count_disagreement' as defect_class, 'measure' as grain, count(*) as defect_count,
        'Measures where this project recounted the published coverage summary and got a different answer.' as detail
    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."data_parity_summary"
    where published_value <> dbt_value
),

combined as (
    select * from date_defects
    union all select * from geocode_defects
    union all select * from weather_defects
    union all select * from flag_defects
    union all select * from topic_defects
    union all select * from time_defects
    union all select * from zone_defects
    union all select * from parity_defects
)

select
    c.defect_class,
    c.grain,
    c.defect_count,
    case when c.grain = 'incident' and t.all_rows > 0
         then c.defect_count * 100.0 / t.all_rows end as pct_of_incidents,
    c.detail
from combined as c
cross join totals as t
where c.defect_count > 0

with all_values as (

    select
        grain as value_field,
        count(*) as n_records

    from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."data_quality_summary"
    group by grain

)

select *
from all_values
where value_field not in (
    'incident','day','zone','topic','flag','measure'
)

select defect_class
from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."data_quality_summary"
where defect_class is null

select
    defect_class as unique_field,
    count(*) as n_records

from "opcrime_dashboard"."main"."data_quality_summary"
where defect_class is not null
group by defect_class
having count(*) > 1
